name: Pacearr v1.0.1 — The Crew Has Names Now
intro:
# The crew has names now. So do the containers. 🏴‍☠️

v1.0.1 replaces development-era deployment names with Pacearr, expands the setup guide and packages the complete source. The public control room gets its first screenshot gallery, while the project’s earlier work stays in the repository.

name: Pacearr v1.0.2 — Nami Sorted the Download Loot
intro:
# Nami sorted the loot. Downloads got organised. 💰

v1.0.2 separates completed sources from files needing attention and makes queued Deluge grabs visible. It also explains client rejections and avoids resubmitting torrents that Deluge has accepted but hasn’t displayed yet.

name: Pacearr v1.0.3 — Franky Checked the Blueprints
intro:
# Franky checked the blueprints. Your folders are next. 🔧

The portable setup release removes assumptions about one person’s NAS. Configure your own mounted folders, account IDs and WebUI port using generic Compose examples, with deployment checks and documentation for new installations.

name: Pacearr v1.1.0 — Only the Episodes You Ordered
intro:
# Sanji doesn’t serve the whole menu when you order five dishes. 🍽️

This feature release selects only requested files from bundles, preserves episode selections and adds scoped download controls. It also introduces 480p support, verified language fallbacks, optional Deluge labels and recovery for completed downloads that were blocked from import.

name: Pacearr v1.1.1 — Even Zoro Could Find the Stop Button
intro:
# Zoro can get lost. Your Stop button shouldn’t. ⚔️

This follow-up to v1.1.0 keeps Stop and Cancel responsive while file work is active. Torrent-metadata attempts are bounded per worker cycle so one unavailable bundle cannot monopolise processing. The complete v1.1.0 feature set is included below.

name: Pacearr v1.1.2 — Brook Came Back. Your Files Can Too
intro:
# Brook came back. Your stranded files can too. 💀

v1.1.2 finds untracked files already in the configured download folder and offers confirmed import recovery. It also preserves failed-grab backoff across automatic checks, caches verified torrent metadata and improves fallback handling instead of repeatedly starting the same request.

name: Pacearr v1.2.0 — Robin Found the Episode Records
intro:
# Robin found the records. Pacearr found the episode. 📚

Official One Pace feeds and direct torrent links join the workflow in v1.2.0. A persistent catalogue remembers episode mappings and historical releases, while verified replacements with unknown installed identities gain an explicit approval action.

name: Pacearr v1.3.0 — A Pocket-Sized Control Room for the Merry
intro:
# The Going Merry got a pocket-sized control room. 🚢

v1.3.0 brings file cards and touch controls to phones, adds bookmark icons and lets you choose the release-check interval. Download reconciliation also keeps unchanged imported sources Completed after torrent removal and gives genuinely absent files a stale-entry action.
